content.comment_body: Hello, I have connected two [product_name] devices together in a master-master setup and am encountering an "EM bus error" message. Does anyone know what this error means or how to resolve it? Thank you [user_name]

Hello [user_name], EM stands for Expansion Module. This error likely indicates a problem with the connection between the main device and its expansion modules. Please check the following: 1) Ensure the connector plug linking the modules is properly and securely connected. 2) Make sure there are not more expansion modules than the device supports. 3) Confirm each expansion module is receiving the required power. If the issue persists, try disconnecting and reconnecting each expansion module individually to identify a faulty one. If you're still unsure, please provide a photo showing how the expansion modules are connected to the main device. Best regards, [user_name]
Hello, In addition to the helpful advice already provided, I've attached a section of the [document]. If all connections seem correct, you might try clearing the alarm to reset the system. Regards,

Hello [user_name] and [user_name], Thank you for helping me resolve this issue. The forum has been very helpful. Yes, EM refers to Expansion Module. The error was caused by having a software program that defined outputs for expansion modules which were not physically connected. Specifically, my client required only a basic module without expansions, but the program had seven outputs instead of four. This mismatch created the error as the program expected outputs from non-existent modules. After removing the extra output assignments, the error was resolved. Thanks again for your support.
Hello, Thank you for your feedback. Regards,

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered an "EM bus error" when connecting two [product_name] devices in a master-master configuration. The issue arose due to the software being set up to use outputs on expansion modules that were not installed, resulting in a system error. The discussion emphasizes the importance of aligning device hardware configuration with the software to prevent such errors and user confusion.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect that hardware and software are properly coordinated, avoiding unclear error messages. Error notifications should give precise information about the source of any faults to facilitate a straightforward resolution.
